newsitem.title: INDIA: Police firing on Indian mob kills two people.
newsitem.headline: Police firing on Indian mob kills two people.

text.p: At least two persons were killed in the Indian capital of New Delhi on Tuesday when police opened fire to combat a rampaging mob protesting against a crackdown on illegal buildings, police said.
A police spokesman said he could not give the number of injured in clashes that took place in a Delhi suburb where police ordered demolition of buildings not recognised by city authorities.
The Press Trust of India (PTI) said 15 people were injured in the clashes, and quoted Delhi's chief minister, Sahib Singh Verma, as saying he had received information of five deaths in the firing.

Police opened fire after it failed to control the crowd of around 15,000 people by using teargas shells and baton charge, PTI said, and quoted a senior police official as saying 31 policemen were injured in the attacks.
The crowd set fire an office of the Delhi Development Authority and a police station, burned vehicles used by paramilitary police and threw stones, PTI said.

The news agency said a crowd of people attacked the police station when they saw bulldozers coming to carry out demolitions ordered by city authorities on buildings constructed without their approval.
